note: A rectified street-panorama crop of one Amsterdam house front; the house in question fills the image.

bands.instructions: Do horizontal light-coloured (white, cream or pale stone) bands run across the brick or painted wall of the house front in `facade`, as continuous courses at floor or window level (speklagen, string courses or continuous lintel bands)? A white cornice at the very top is not a band.

criteria.true: One or more continuous horizontal light bands cross the wall.
criteria.false: The wall has no continuous horizontal light band; only separate lintels or sills, or nothing.

surrounds.instructions: Are the upper-storey windows of the house front in `facade` framed by a white or cream painted surround or stone frame on the wall, wider than the window frame itself (jambs and lintel in a light colour contrasting with the wall)?

criteria.true: A light surround or architrave frames the windows against a darker wall.
criteria.false: The windows sit directly in the wall; only the glazing bars may be white, or the frames are dark.

keystones.instructions: Do the upper-storey windows of the house front in `facade` have keystones or decorative stones at the centre of the lintel or arch above each window?

criteria.true: Keystones or ornaments sit above the windows.

quoins.instructions: Does the house front in `facade` have light quoins (corner stones: alternating light stone blocks running up the sides of the front)?

criteria.true: Light quoin blocks run up the corners.

cornice.instructions: Is the cornice or parapet at the top of the house front in `facade` painted white or cream (a wide, light horizontal moulding under the roof)?

criteria.true: A white or cream cornice or parapet band tops the front.
criteria.false: The top of the front is brick, dark, or has no light cornice, or the top is not visible.
